subject: Regional infill + burst capacity plan for NimbusAI APAC commitment
messages:
From: Rita Chen <rita@nimbus.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning for APAC dedicated pool — NimbusAI Q3 commitment

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick summary / ask from our side: NimbusAI is targeting a firm Q3 commitment for APAC traffic (we run a global search+chat stack). We expect an initial steady-state average of ~7.5k concurrent requests (95th pctl) across APAC with peak events that could spike ~3–4x on product launch days. Token mix is heavy on short-form chat (~15 tokens/request avg) but a small fraction (5%) are long-context reranks (~4k tokens).

High-level ask: can Redwood size a recommended Dedicated pool for APAC that covers a conservative baseline (sustained SLA) plus a burst plan for launch spikes? We prefer a tranche-based reservation (baseline + option to burst on-demand or via guaranteed burst credits). Curious about lead times for reserved capacity, typical pre-buy discounts, and any constraints on cross-AZ bursting in Singapore / Sydney zones.

I attached our traffic projection (nimbus_expected_traffic_by_month.csv) and a copy of the MOU (signed_mou_draft_v2.pdf) — the commercial team wants to lock an outline this week. Can you loop in the capacity team and provide a recommended baseline + burst sizing, plus a short ramp schedule?

Also copying procurement who may join for contract/pricing specifics.

Thanks — Rita
Rita Chen
Head of Platform Operations, NimbusAI
rita@nimbus.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Chen <rita@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for APAC dedicated pool — NimbusAI Q3 commitment

Hi Rita — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Looping Ben (commercial lead) and Marissa (capacity planning) to size this correctly. Quick checklist from our side so we size baseline vs burst accurately:

- Confirmed region footprint: is traffic concentrated in Singapore and Sydney or do you expect substantial Hong Kong/Tokyo demand?
- Concurrency breakdown by AZ (if available).
- Percent of requests requiring long-context / KV-cacheable workloads vs short streaming responses.
- Desired SLOs for baseline vs burst (p50/p95 latency targets; drop/queue policy at peak).
- Any regulatory requirement for data residency or private deployment in APAC.

Initial tranche proposal (high level, ballpark):
- Baseline reserved pool: capacity equivalent to ~20 A100-40GB GPUs sustained (handles steady-state 95th pctl)
- Guaranteed burst tranche: additional 25-30 GPUs equivalent available for 4–12 hour windows (auto-allocated when policy triggers)
- Fallback path: stream to lower-cost quantized model variants if burst capacity is exhausted (we can define per-route fallbacks)

Lead times: reserved capacity (for firm committed GPUs) typically requires ~3–6 weeks depending on AZ and SKU availability; burst credits are immediate once configured but guaranteed burst (reserved-on-call) needs a shorter provisioning window (~7–14 days) to warm nodes. Marissa, can you confirm concretely for Singapore & Sydney?

I attached a short APAC burst options workbook (apac-burst-sla-options.xlsx) that outlines pricing shapes and SLAs — Ben, please pick up pricing.

Next steps: Marissa to propose an engineering-backed sizing + ramp, Ben to provide price tiers and discount schedule, then we can propose a 2-week mutual action plan for signatures.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

Rita / Priya — quick commercial note while Marissa sizes:

Pricing tranches (illustrative):
- Baseline reserved: $0.90 / GPU-hour (A100-40GB equivalent) for 12-month commit; volume discounts at >5000 GPU-hours/mo
- Guaranteed burst tranche: $1.35 / GPU-hour for on-call reserved capacity (minimum monthly guarantee)
- On-demand burst (best-effort): $1.95 / GPU-hour (no SLA)

Example commitment: baseline = ~20 GPUs sustained (month 1–3), burst reserve = 25 GPUs for 12 months, with a ramp to 40 baseline GPUs by month 6 if usage growth matches projections. We can offer one-time onboarding credits (equivalent to 2000 GPU-hours) if legal signs the attached MOU this week.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Capacity planning for APAC dedicated pool — NimbusAI Q3 commitment

Thanks all — I ran the projections against our provisioning matrix and here's a pragmatic, engineering-backed plan for APAC (Singapore primary, Sydney secondary). I included constraints and an initial ramp schedule below.

Recommendation (baseline + burst):
- Baseline reserved: equivalent to 18 A100-40GB GPUs (sustained) split across 2 AZs (SGN-a: 10, SYD-a: 8). This covers the 95th pctl for the profile in your CSV assuming the short-form model is used for 95% of requests and the long-context model is routed to separate nodes.
- Guaranteed burst pool: reserve an additional 28 GPUs in a warm pool (pooled across AZs) that can be guaranteed for 4–12 hour windows; warm pool uses pre-warmed instances to hit latency SLOs when activated.
- Cold on-demand capacity: access to cloud spot-backed nodes for >12 hour sustained spikes (best-effort).

Operational notes / constraints:
- Lead time: for reserved GPUs in SGN, expect ~21 business days for firm provisioning of the baseline. Guaranteed burst warm pool requires ~7–10 business days to validate warm images & policies.
- Cross-AZ scaling: automatic cross-AZ failover is supported but sustained cross-AZ burst will incur additional networking egress and slightly higher p95 latency; we recommend routing by region-preference first.
- Cost/efficiency levers: prefix caching for frequent prompts and model quantization for non-critical routes can reduce baseline GPU needs by up to ~18% in our sims.

Ramp schedule (example):
- Week 0 (sign MOU): allocate capacity reservation request to infra (baseline 18 GPUs + 28 warm burst credits).
- Weeks 1–3: provisioning of baseline nodes in SGN/SYD; pre-warm burst images and run load validation with Nimbus test tokens (we'd need an allowlisted test key).
- Week 4: soft cutover to baseline for 50% traffic, monitor p95/p99 and token-costs.
- Month 2–3: increase baseline to 25 GPUs if real traffic tracks projections; fully enable guaranteed burst windows for launch events.

Attachments: I uploaded the APAC sizing workbook (apac-burst-sla-options.xlsx) with the node mapping, failover plan, and a short checklist for on-call burst activation.

If this looks good I'll formalize a mutual action plan doc and share a provisioning RFC for infra. Priya / Ben — recommend we lock MOU signature this week to meet a mid-May soft launch.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Capacity & Distributed Systems, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
